Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 22-Jun-2024 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  SECOND SEMESTER B.TECH. EXAMINATIONS - JUNE 2024  
  SUBJECT: MIE 1071/MIE_1071 - BASIC MECHANICAL ENGINEERING  
  BASIC MECHANICAL ENGINEERING [MIE 1071-PHY]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)                1200 kg of 28.75% wet steam is produced in a coal-fired boiler at a pressure of 1.2 MPa. The feed (4)  
  water to the boiler is supplied from a reservoir maintained at a temperature of 30°C. The steam  
  from the boiler is then sent into a superheater where it is heated to a temperature of 210°C. During  
  this passage from boiler to superheater, the steam condenses and loses 760 MJ of heat. Find the  
  following:  
  i) Total heat supplied in the boiler.  
  ii) Dryness fraction of the steam at the entry of superheater  
  iii) Total heat supplied in the superheater.  
1B)                A food processing industry operating a water tube boiler, uses 15% wet steam at a temperature of       (3)  
  165°C. The industry has a choice of using wood chips or powdered coal having calorific values of  
  22 MJ/kg and 30 MJ/kg respectively for firing the boiler. The boiler is to be operated at an average  
  efficiency of 80%. Determine the percentage saving in the quantity of fuel used if coal powder is  
  selected. The steam requirement is 750 kg/day using the feed water at a temperature of 32°C.  
1C)                Explain the significance of the following mountings:                                                   (3)  
  i) Pressure gauge  
  ii) Safety valve  
  iii) Fusible plug  
2A)                An assembly line uses a belt drive to transfer power from an electric motor to a conveyor belt. The (4)  
  diameter of the motor pulley is 300 mm, and the conveyor belt pulley which is to run in a direction  
  opposite to the motor pulley is designed to have a velocity ratio of 1/3. The centre distance between  
  the two pulleys is 1 m, and the coefficient of friction between the belt and the pulleys is estimated to  
  be 0.25.  
  Given these parameters:  
  Infer the type of belt drive used and hence calculate the length of the belt required for this drive  
  system. Also determine the power transmitted by the belt drive if the motor runs at 1440 rpm and  
  the initial tension in the belt drive when stationary is 800 N  
2B)                An industrial machine uses a combination of a crossed belt drive and a compound gear train for its (3)  
  operation. The initial speed reduction is achieved through a crossed belt drive system, and further  
  reduction is done using a compound gear train with four shafts.  
  The crossed belt drive consists of a driver pulley with a diameter of 250 mm and a driven pulley with  
  a diameter of 500 mm. The centre distance between the pulleys is 1.5 meters, and the driver pulley  
  rotates at 1200 RPM.  
  
  The compound gear train includes four shafts with the following gear specifications:  
  
  • Shaft 1: Gear A (Driver) - 20 teeth  
  • Shaft 2: Gear B - 40 teeth, Gear C - 18 teeth (mounted on the same shaft as Gear B)  
  
  
  Page 1 of 2

• Shaft 3: Gear D - 44 teeth, Gear E - 22 teeth (mounted on the same shaft as Gear D)  
  • Shaft 4: Gear F (Driven) - 46 teeth  
  
  Meshing of gears is as follows: Gear A with Gear B, Gear C with Gear D, and Gear E with Gear F.  
  Determine the velocity ratio of the compound gear train and the speed of the driven shaft. Sketch  
  the arrangement.  
2C)   A factory operates a belt-driven system to transmit power from a motor to various machines. The       (3)  
  system should include a pulley arrangement that allows intermittent switching Off and On, of select  
  machines. Analyse the given scenario and identify the type of pulley involved. Explain the working  
  principle of the same with the help of a neat sketch.  
3A)   The following observations were recorded during a test on a 4-stroke engine. Bore=25cm, Stroke        (4)  
  =40cm, Cam Shaft Speed= 125 rpm, Mean effective pressure= 6bar, Fuel consumption=  
  0.0013kg/sec, Calorific value of the fuel= 43900kJ/kg. Effective brake load = 50 kg, Mean  
  circumference of brake drum = 4 m. Determine the indicated thermal efficiency and brake thermal  
  efficiency.  
3B)   Sketch and explain the working principle of an engine fitted with a carburetor and is cranked by a    (3)  
  lighter flywheel.  
3C)   Give reasons for the following:                                                                       (3)  
  i) Diesel engines have higher compression ratio  
  ii) Four stroke engines are costlier in comparison to two stroke engines  
  iii) Piston rings are an essential part of the piston  
4A)   With suitable sketches, explain tapping, reaming, counter-sinking and counter-boring operations.      (4)  
4B)   Explain the function of saddle, compound rest and feed rod in lathe machine.                          (3)  
4C)   Explain any six advantages of CNC machine.                                                            (3)  
5A)   Explain any four desirable characteristics of moulding sand.                                          (4)  
5B)   With neat sketches, briefly explain the characteristics of various Oxy-Acetylene flame used in gas    (3)  
  welding.  
5C)   Explain the limitations associated with punched tape and tape readers of NC machine.                  (3)  
  
  
  -----End-----
